speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the specific location and nature of your neck and arm pain, and does it radiate down a particular arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts or writing, and does the pain worsen when you extend your neck? Also, have you noticed any changes in your bowel or bladder control, or any numbness in your saddle area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and bilateral hand weakness, I am concerned about lower motor neuron involvement. REQUEST TEST: EMG_NCS.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the EMG is normal, the fasciculations and weakness are likely not due to primary motor neuron disease like ALS. I need to rule out structural compression or peripheral neuropathy. Can you confirm if the weakness is symmetrical and if you have any sensory loss in a "glove and stocking" distribution, and REQUEST TEST: MRI_Cervical_Spine.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI of the cervical spine reveals a syrinx (cavity) within the spinal cord extending from the cervical to the upper thoracic region.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms a syrinx extending from the cervical to upper thoracic region. Do you have any history of severe head or neck trauma, or symptoms suggestive of Chiari malformation such as headaches worsened by coughing or straining?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of trauma suggests post-traumatic syringomyelia, but your inconsistent condom use raises concern for neurosyphilis. I will order specific serology to rule out infectious causes. REQUEST TEST: VDRL_RPR, REQUEST TEST: CSF_VDRL

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative syphilis serology effectively rules out neurosyphilis, confirming the diagnosis of post-traumatic syringomyelia secondary to your motor vehicle accident. DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-traumatic Syringomyelia
